blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fluorouracil hand-foot syndrome recognition
stem: A client receiving continuous-infusion fluorouracil develops painful redness and swelling of both palms and soles with tingling and tenderness. Which interpretation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: These findings are consistent with fluorouracil-associated hand-foot syndrome and should be reported for supportive care and severity-based treatment reassessment.
options.B: These findings indicate a favorable antitumor response and support continuing treatment without medication-related assessment or symptom-focused evaluation.
options.C: These findings are unlikely to be fluorouracil related because palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia is not a recognized toxicity of continuous-infusion therapy.
options.D: These findings reflect improved peripheral circulation and can be observed without treatment reassessment unless another systemic symptom develops.

rationale: Current fluorouracil labeling states that palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (hand-foot syndrome) can cause tingling, pain, swelling, erythema with tenderness, and desquamation and is more common with continuous infusion than bolus dosing. Supportive measures are recommended; Grade 2 or 3 HFS requires withholding treatment until improvement, with dose reduction on resumption. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize painful erythema, swelling, tenderness, and tingling of palms/soles as fluorouracil hand-foot syndrome requiring prompt reporting and severity-based management.
source_version_date: Current 2026 DailyMed label; revised January 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §5.6 Palmar-Plantar Erythrodysesthesia: tingling, pain, swelling, erythema with tenderness, desquamation; more common with continuous infusion; supportive care; withhold Grade 2/3 and resume reduced dose after resolution/improvement.
source_claim_supported: Fluorouracil can cause hand-foot syndrome with painful erythema/swelling/tingling, especially with continuous infusion, and clinically significant cases require treatment reassessment.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: recognize medication-related skin toxicity, assess severity, provide supportive care, and report findings requiring treatment modification.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Balanced all options as complete interpretations of the same palm/sole findings and removed the uniquely-long key cue.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current fluorouracil labeling and option lengths are tightly balanced.
